title: Assessment Frequency in MYP Standard Mathematics
summary: Learn how often MYP Standard Mathematics assessments should occur, what the IB requires, and how schools can balance formative and summative tasks.
body_markdown:
Assessment frequency in MYP Standard Mathematics is **not fixed by the IB as a weekly, monthly, or termly number** . Schools set their own calendars, but they must gather enough evidence to judge every strand of all four mathematics criteria at least twice during the year. In practice, this usually means regular formative checks and a substantial summative task near the end of each unit.


### What the IB actually requires


MYP assessment is primarily school-based. According to the[IB overview of MYP assessment](https://www.ibo.org/programmes/middle-years-programme/assessment-and-exams/) , teachers design and mark varied tasks using prescribed subject-group criteria.


MYP mathematics has four equally weighted criteria:


- **Criterion A: Knowing and understanding**
- **Criterion B: Investigating patterns**
- **Criterion C: Communicating**
- **Criterion D: Applying mathematics in real-life contexts**


The requirement concerns criterion coverage, not a fixed number of tests. Schools must provide valid opportunities to assess all strands of each criterion at least twice during the year. The[official MYP mathematics subject brief](https://www.ibo.org/globalassets/new-structure/brochures-and-infographics/pdfs/myp-brief-mathematics-en.pdf) outlines what each criterion measures.


One task can assess multiple criteria. For example, an investigation might assess **Criterion B** through pattern generalisation and **Criterion C** through notation and reasoning. Assessing four criteria twice therefore does not require eight separate tests.


### A practical assessment schedule


The following pattern is a practical recommendation, not an IB rule.


Assessment type Sensible frequency Main purpose


Diagnostic check Start of a unit or major topic Identify prior knowledge and misconceptions


Informal formative check Once or several times weekly Adjust teaching and provide immediate feedback


Substantial formative task One or two per unit Rehearse skills and assessment criteria


Summative assessment Usually once per unit Record evidence against selected criteria


Cumulative review Once per term or before examinations Check retention across topics


With six-to-eight-week units, a class might complete **four to six summative assessments per year** . Longer units may produce fewer, broader tasks, while shorter units may produce more. Either approach can work if criteria are covered and students have time to use feedback.


### Formative assessment should be frequent


Formative assessment is assessment **for learning** . It may include exit tickets, short quizzes, questioning, worked examples, mini-whiteboard responses, self-assessment, or teacher observation during problem solving.


These checks do not always need reported grades. They reveal misconceptions before those weaknesses obstruct later topics, which is particularly important with foundational ideas such as fractions, algebra, and proportional reasoning.


Students can use[MYP Standard Mathematics Study Notes](https://www.revisiondojo.com/myp/myp-standard-mathematics/notes) to revisit a weak concept, then complete targeted questions from the[MYP Standard Mathematics Questionbank](https://www.revisiondojo.com/myp/myp-standard-mathematics/questionbank) . This turns assessment evidence into focused improvement rather than general revision.


### Summative assessment should be purposeful


Summative tasks evaluate achievement after sufficient teaching, practice, and feedback. They should not assess only calculation speed or memorised procedures because MYP mathematics also evaluates investigation, communication, and application.


A balanced programme might include:


- Unit tests assessing Criteria A and C
- Pattern investigations assessing Criteria B and C
- Modelling tasks assessing Criteria C and D
- Cumulative assessments combining several criteria


Varied formats allow students to demonstrate different forms of mathematical understanding. RevisionDojo’s guide to[how MYP Mathematics is assessed](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-myp-mathematics-is-assessed-and-how-to-revise-for-it) explains how each criterion affects a successful response.


### Signs that assessment is too frequent


More assessment does not automatically produce stronger evidence. The schedule may be excessive if students move between graded tasks without time to understand feedback, correct errors, or practise independently.


Warning signs include:


- Major graded tasks occur weekly without a clear criterion-based purpose.
- Feedback arrives after the next assessment.
- Most tasks assess Criterion A while investigations and applications remain rare.
- Test preparation repeatedly replaces new learning.
- Several subjects schedule major deadlines together.


Assessment may be too infrequent if students receive no feedback for most of a term, meet a criterion for the first time in a summative task, or receive grades based on limited evidence.


### What students and parents should ask


Rather than asking only how many tests will occur, students and parents should request the assessment calendar and criterion-coverage plan. Useful questions include:


- Which criteria and strands will each task assess?
- Will every strand be assessed at least twice?
- What formative practice comes before the summative task?
- How quickly will actionable feedback arrive?
- Will students have another opportunity to demonstrate progress?


Between assessments, students should review feedback, identify one precise weakness, relearn the concept, and complete focused questions. The[MYP Mathematics study techniques guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/best-study-techniques-for-myp-mathematics) offers a criterion-focused method, while the[MYP Standard Mathematics resource hub](https://www.revisiondojo.com/myp/myp-standard-mathematics) combines notes, practice questions, flashcards, and exam-building tools.


### Conclusion


There is no universal IB rule requiring a weekly test or a fixed number of assessments per term. Appropriate assessment frequency means **ongoing formative checking, meaningful practice within each unit, and purposeful summative evidence** .


The schedule should cover all four criteria without crowding out teaching, feedback, and improvement. RevisionDojo Study Notes, the Questionbank, Flashcards, and Jojo AI can help students address weaknesses identified through classroom assessment.
